To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency and properties of active galactic nucleus (AGN) activity in group galaxies, down to luminosities of a few times 1040 erg s−1, can be studied with X-ray observations unaffected by obscuration and dilution by the host galaxy.
the fraction of central galaxies hosting AGN activity is higher than that of satellites of comparable mass, and that the frequency of AGN activity does not depend on distance to the group center.

the frequency of active galactic nucleus (AGN) activity in central group galaxies is higher than that in satellite galaxies of similar stellar mass and that the rate of AGN decline with redshift matches the rate of decline for the overall AGN population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the X-ray emission from the hot gas in nearby groups and the X-ray emission of AGNs in the group environment.
the study of active galactic nuclear (AGN) activity in galaxies in nearby galaxy groups.
the study of the evolution of AGN activity and its connection to galaxy and group evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AGN activity is a function of the galaxy mass, not the halo mass, and the frequency of AGN activity is independent of halo-centric distance for satellites of similar mass.
AGNs are found preferentially in the most massive central galaxies of groups and halos, and that their frequency declines with increasing redshift.

AGN activity in group galaxies is not a strong function of halo-centric position or group mass, but rather a strong function of galaxy mass, with the AGN activity rate declining with decreasing galaxy mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AGN activity in group halos is a function of the mass of the central galaxy and that the rate of AGN activity does not appear to be affected by halo mass or redshift.

the frequency of AGN activity, as traced by X-ray emission, in galaxy groups is consistent with the occupation fraction of AGNs in galaxy groups being similar to that in the field, with the AGN activity being driven by galaxy mass and not halo mass.
the X-ZENS data are consistent with the AGN population being distributed randomly within group halos, and that AGN evolution is not strongly dependent on halo mass. © 2018 The Author(s).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the X-ray properties of AGN activity, in particular the luminosity function, are consistent with the picture of a population of central galaxies that is preferentially more massive than satellite galaxies and a population of satellite galaxies that are preferentially more massive at higher redshift.

the X-ray properties of the AGN population in galaxy groups are similar to those of AGNs in field galaxies of the same mass and redshift, and that the frequency of AGN activity does not depend on halo mass.
the AGN occupation of galaxy halos is not strongly dependent on halo-centric distance, but rather on the galaxy mass and morphological type.
